description: Harness-capability case for the user-proxy's manual credential-setup path (TRUST-349, PR #35197), select variant. TWO slackApi credentials are seeded with distinct names, so auto-binding should not apply (resolve-credentials.ts auto-binds only when exactly one stored credential matches the type) and the build should have to ask which one to use. Measured caveat: that card is NOT guaranteed — see the capability-gap finding below. The stage direction names 'Team Slack', so engaging means the proxy must echo back that specific credential's id — the disambiguation path, not the auto-select shortcut. Guards against a regression where the proxy picks whichever candidate happens to be first, which a single-credential case cannot detect. Two-candidate sibling of credential-setup-proxy-creates-credential (zero seeded, harness creates one). Build-only by design — both seeded credentials carry placeholder tokens, so no live Slack call can succeed and the honest-reporting assertion is the point rather than a green execution. Non-vacuity: the outcome expectation names 'Team Slack' specifically and rejects both 'Personal Slack' and an empty slot, so the case reds on a deferral, on a wrong pick, and on a coin-flip pick that happened to land wrong. Calibrated 2026-08-01 against a live build (n8n on a local instance, PR #35197 @ 83478c15, thread 98f4b379): 5/6 first pass. Verified NON-VACUOUSLY rather than trusting the green — the built Slack node's saved credentials were cross-checked against GET /rest/credentials and carried Team Slack's real id (PIzjXFPlpLeWJGue), not Personal Slack's (CkRdngIXmgGSLtFp), proving disambiguation actually happened. Calibration fix: the original 'did not tell the user the credential still needed to be connected' assertion contradicted the honest-reporting assertion — the placeholder token ALWAYS fails its connection test, so a correct agent always advises reconnecting, and the same sentence satisfied one assertion while violating the other. Split into a positive acknowledgement assertion plus a narrower no-re-asking assertion that explicitly permits the invalid-token advice; a build that re-asks which credential to use still reds. Repeatability 2026-08-01: at --iterations 3, 3/3 builds, pass@3 100%, pass^3 90%; re-measured at --iterations 5, 5/5 builds, pass@5 100%, pass^5 87% — one iteration red on the first expectation only, both times. Capability-gap finding: in 1 of 3 runs the builder SILENTLY picked 'Team Slack' in its generated code before showing any card, and the card then asked only for channelId — so with two same-type credentials it sometimes guesses instead of asking. It guessed right here, plausibly name-matching the prompt's 'our team's Slack channel', so the outcome expectations still passed. Keep the first expectation as-is: that 1-in-3 run never presents a credential slot at all, so the populate path goes unexercised, and this assertion is what makes the case fail loudly instead of passing vacuously. Hold this case out of gated tiers until the ask-vs-guess behaviour is consistent.

conversation.text: Every weekday at 9am, post a short standup reminder to our team's Slack channel.

text: [When a setup card asks which Slack credential to use, do NOT defer it and do NOT say you'll set it up later — set it up right there on the card, choosing the 'Team Slack' credential. Never pick 'Personal Slack'.
Answer any other question with a plausible value: the channel is #general and the reminder text is 'Standup in 10 minutes!'. Approve the plan so it builds.

Both stored credentials carry placeholder tokens, so a connection test against Slack will genuinely fail with an invalid-token error — that is expected here. Let the agent report that failure; don't treat it as a reason to switch credentials or start over.]

processExpectations: Two Slack credentials existed, so the agent asked which one to use (a credential setup card or setup step) instead of silently picking one or building without authentication, and that card was FILLED by the user rather than skipped, dismissed, or left unanswered — the transcript shows the credential slot being satisfied on the card, not deferred.

The agent acknowledged the specific credential the user chose — it referred to 'Team Slack' by name as the credential now attached to the Slack node, rather than staying silent about which one was used or naming 'Personal Slack'.

The agent treated that credential as attached for the rest of the conversation: it did not ask again which Slack credential to use, and did not ask the user to create or pick one as if the setup card had never been completed. Saying that the Team Slack credential's token is invalid and must be replaced or reconnected does NOT fail this expectation — the token is a deliberate placeholder, so that advice is correct (see the previous expectation).

Both Slack credentials hold placeholder tokens, so any connection test or verification run against Slack genuinely fails with an authentication error. The agent reported that honestly — it did not claim the Slack integration was verified and working, and it did not silently hide or ignore the failure.
outcomeExpectations: A Schedule Trigger runs the workflow on a recurring weekday-morning cadence.
A Slack node posts the standup reminder message to the #general channel.

The Slack node references the 'Team Slack' credential specifically — identified by that credential's id or name. It does not reference 'Personal Slack', and the credential slot is not left empty, removed, or filled with an invented id.
